title: Grateful Dead Live at Pacific Recording Studios on 1969-06-20
lineage: A>D transfer: Linn LP12/Lingo turntable, Linn Ittok tonearm, Lyra Helikon cartridge,PS Audio PCA-2 preamplifier, M Audio Audiophile USB external, A/C powered sound card
source: Ampex 16-track tape > LP > 24-bit, 44.1 kHz WAV > 16-bit, 44.1 kHz WAV > SHN

ai_review.summary: Original 1969 Aoxomoxoa mix streams with clear studio sound and highlights like “What’s Become of the Baby,” “Cosmic Charlie,” and a vivid China Cat intro.
ai_review.review: The archive entry provides the original 1969 mix of Aoxomoxoa, which many reviewers say sounds clearer and more adventurous than the later 1971 remix. Listeners appreciate standout tracks such as “What’s Become of the Baby,” “Cosmic Charlie,” “Doin’ That Rag,” and an especially memorable intro to “China Cat Sunflower,” though a few note occasional pops at the end of that track. Overall the recording is praised for its fidelity, with only minor imperfections.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers (8+ out of 15) give 4–5 stars and praise the original mix’s sound quality and song highlights; only a few low‑star comments detract minimally, leading to a strong positive rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Original 1969 studio mix; clearer and more dynamic than the 1971 remix. Some listeners note occasional pops/skips at the end of “China Cat Sunflower.”

show_quality.setlist_flow: Studio album flow with classic Aoxomoxoa sequencing; no live set structure to comment on.
